learningObjectives: Review design values before generating executable tests.
Distinguish Specific filling from Orthogonal filling and inspect active filters.
Use custom values where an Attribute has no defined Instances.
Link a data source to a template and verify generated XL paths.

elements.description: Generated combinations still need the input, metadata and expected values required by your test implementation. Independent Administration/Verification labels describe their intended purpose; filling them does not by itself create or execute assertions.

elements.text: Inspect the resulting dataset after changing values or structure. Do not assume an unchanged row count proves that every association and expected outcome is still correct.

bulletPoints: TestSheet data and an executable TestCase Template are distinct artifacts.

elements.description: The documented Fill empty Values → Specific action fills empty fields using a selected value; if an Attribute has no Instances, you can supply a custom value. Orthogonal filling instead uses child Instance values. Confirm the target selection and the resulting fields before generating tests.

bulletPoints: Filling empty fields does not imply overwriting already populated values.

elements.term: When one value per row isn't enough
elements.description: Independent example: use different stage labels for selected tests according to your plan. Boundary checks can belong in regression; they are not automatically one-time tests.
Add the Filter column with Column Chooser to filter Instances at TestSheet or Attribute level. Inspect the active selection and resulting values rather than relying only on display color.

elements.text: Hovering over the TestSheet shows filtered values. Remove an active filter with Reset Instances Filter. Verify intended data edits; these source pages do not establish that every bulk-fill command is confined by the current visibility filter.

bulletPoints: Filters change the displayed subset. They are not a guarantee about the mutation scope of every command.
Reset filters and inspect the complete dataset before reporting it complete.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Direct values and template data binding

elements.description: The dynamic-menu reference allows a user-specific value when an Attribute has no Instances. Confirm that the selected data scope and intended row agree; the previous blanket claim that higher-level entry always corrupts combinations is not established by the accessed documentation.

For automated tests, link the TestSheet or Class to a TestCase Template. SchemaName identifies the linked source. Automatic XL paths require empty TestStepValues whose names uniquely match Attributes; manually check those paths before creating the TemplateInstance.

bulletPoints: Do not confuse filling design data, binding a template and executing generated tests.

elements.text: Independent checklist: inspect actual values, clear accidental filters, check expected results and XL paths, then generate and inspect the executable tests. Original Academy video/exercises require authentication and were not reviewed.

examPitfalls.title: Filling versus overwriting
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming an empty-field operation overwrites every existing value.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect empty and already populated cells; use the documented Specific/Orthogonal behavior deliberately.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a filter limits every edit
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a visible subset as proof of a bulk operation’s mutation scope.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Confirm results across the complete dataset after the edit; reset the Instances Filter.

examPitfalls.title: Automatic template mapping
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting a filled or ambiguously named TestStepValue to receive the intended XL path.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Automatic XL paths require empty TestStepValues with uniquely matching names, followed by manual inspection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The selected design scope has empty Test Designer fields that should all receive 'Max Methodology'. Which documented operation fits?

options.text: Click each cell individually and type the name.
Use Fill empty Values → Specific and supply the intended value, then inspect the results.
Use the Filter Column, since one value is needed for the whole row.
Convert Administration into a Value Attribute.

practiceQuiz.hint: One value, applied to every empty cell in the row, in one action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Specific filling supplies a selected/custom value to empty fields. It does not imply that existing values are overwritten or that the template is already bound.

optionExplanations.A: Manual filling is possible but repeats the same empty-field work.
optionExplanations.B: Specific filling matches a shared selected value for empty fields.
optionExplanations.C: A filter selects a view; it does not itself populate values.
optionExplanations.D: Changing object structure is unnecessary for the documented filling action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A design needs different stage labels for selected test rows. Which approach avoids assuming a view filter alone makes bulk edits safe?

options.text: Use Fill Empty Values → Specific twice, once for each value.
Inspect the selected Instances, assign the intended labels and verify the complete dataset after clearing filters.
This cannot be done — every cell in a row must share one value.
Delete and recreate the Attribute for each subset.

practiceQuiz.hint: Visibility and mutation scope are different concerns.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Filters help inspect a subset, but the accessed reference does not certify the mutation scope of every bulk operation. Verify the actual complete data after assigning values.

optionExplanations.A: Repeating a whole-scope fill does not deliberately assign distinct row labels.
optionExplanations.B: Explicit assignment plus full-data verification checks the intended associations.
optionExplanations.C: The design can contain different values across tests.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting Attributes is unnecessary and can lose existing structure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After using the Filter column, how can a tester remove the Instances Filter and inspect the full design?

options.text: Use Reset Instances Filter on the TestSheet or Attribute.

practiceQuiz.hint: Filtering has a documented reset action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Reset Instances Filter removes the view filter. It does not require deletion, relevance changes or license configuration.

optionExplanations.A: Hidden data need not be deleted to remove a filter.
optionExplanations.B: The documented reset action clears the filter.
optionExplanations.C: Business relevance and display filtering are separate.
optionExplanations.D: Licensing does not reset an Instances Filter.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For automatic XL path creation after linking a TestSheet to a template, what does the documentation require?

options.text: Every TestStepValue must already contain a constant.
Empty TestStepValues with names uniquely matching the source Attributes; manually verify the resulting paths.
Filtering the source automatically executes and maps the test.

practiceQuiz.hint: Check empty values and unique name matching.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The reference requires empty TestStepValues and uniquely matching names for generated XL paths, then manual checks. Linking is not execution.

optionExplanations.A: Existing constants prevent the stated automatic empty-value mapping.
optionExplanations.B: Empty fields and unique matching names are the documented prerequisites.
optionExplanations.C: Name matching is explicitly part of automatic path creation.
optionExplanations.D: Filtering neither executes the test nor ensures correct mapping.

quickRecap.value: Supply a selected/custom value for empty fields; verify the resulting scope.
Inspect selected data, then reset and review the complete dataset.
Supported when an Attribute has no defined Instances; validate the intended data association.
Empty TestStepValues and unique Attribute-name matches permit automatic XL paths; manually inspect them.
Filling data, binding a template and executing tests are different operations.
